evidence_spans: CSI-based training uses 5440 blocks (32 640 RF vectors) and reaches 91.8% test accuracy on 8192 test blocks.
In simulation, uncorrected training fails in negative correlation lobes and revives in positive ones.
CLM-ARCH-0099.statement: CSI-based training reaches a test accuracy of 91.8%.

evidence_spans: For the isotropic spectrum (Fig. 1), uncorrected training collapses in the first negative lobe (36.2% at d = 0.55) and revives in the second positive lobe (89.4% at d = 1.05, matching phase correction to one decimal).
In simulation, uncorrected training fails in negative correlation lobes and revives in positive ones.
CLM-ARCH-0100.statement: Uncorrected training achieves a test accuracy of 36.2% at a displacement of d = 0.55 for the isotropic spectrum.

extra_quotes: We train eight equiprobable messages over four channel uses with N t = 2 and a single receive antenna.
The transmitter learns a 2×4 codebook per message with unit-norm columns; the receiver learns a softmax classifier on the 16 real features of the temporal Gram matrix of the received block.
Forward and reverse noise variances are 0.10 and 0.0009 (the latter added before norm restoration); encoder and receiver use Adam with learning rates 0.01 and 0.03.

Limitations. The rotation statement is exact for the conditional-mean port-domain return under our single-antenna Gaussian model; the lobe, waiting and few-bit results are simulations, not a convergence theorem.
